description: Every pane of Edit > Preferences (Ctrl+K) with its key options, the performance-related settings (memory, GPU, history, cache, scratch disks), preference reset and scripting access, plus the colour-management commands (Color Settings sections, Assign/Convert Profile, soft proofing, gamut warning, rendering intents) and Content Credentials.

tools.name: Preferences > General
tools.description: Top-level behaviour switches: which Color Picker to use (Adobe or Windows/Mac), HUD Color Picker style, the default Image Interpolation for transforms, the Home screen, legacy New Document dialog, Export Clipboard, Resize Image During Place, Skip Transform when Placing, Beep When Done, warning-dialog reset and 'Reset Preferences On Quit'.

parameters.name: Color Picker
parameters.description: Adobe (default) or the OS picker.

parameters.name: HUD Color Picker
parameters.description: Hue Strip or Hue Wheel, small/medium/large (Shift+Alt+right-click on canvas).

parameters.name: Image Interpolation
parameters.description: Default resampling for Free Transform and Image Size: Bicubic Automatic, Bicubic, Bicubic Smoother, Bicubic Sharper, Bilinear, Nearest Neighbor, Preserve Details 2.0.

parameters.name: Auto Show the Home Screen / Use Legacy 'New Document' Interface
parameters.description: Start-up and New dialog behaviour.

parameters.name: Export Clipboard
parameters.description: Make copied pixels available to other apps on switch (slows switching for large clips).

parameters.name: Resize Image During Place / Skip Transform when Placing
parameters.description: Fit placed files to the canvas; skip the transform step.

parameters.name: Reset All Warning Dialogs / Reset Preferences On Quit
parameters.description: Re-enable 'don't show again' dialogs; wipe prefs at next quit.

tools.example: Set Image Interpolation to Bicubic Sharper if most of your transforms reduce size, and untick Export Clipboard when copying huge selections to speed up app switching.
tools.notes: ExtendScript: `app.preferences.colorPicker`, `app.preferences.interpolation = ResampleMethod.BICUBIC`, `app.preferences.exportClipboard`. Preferences are written when Photoshop quits.

tools.name: Preferences > Interface
tools.description: Controls the look of the application: the four Color Theme greys, the highlight colour, the canvas colour and border for each screen mode, whether channels show in colour, menu colours, dynamic colour sliders, and UI language, font size and UI scaling.

parameters.name: Color Theme / Highlight Color
parameters.description: Darkest to lightest grey; highlight Default (grey) or Blue.

parameters.name: Standard / Full Screen with Menus / Full Screen
parameters.description: Canvas colour (Default, Black, Dark Gray, Medium Gray, Light Gray, White, Custom) and border (Line, Drop Shadow, None) per screen mode.

parameters.name: Show Channels in Color / Show Menu Colors / Dynamic Color Sliders
parameters.description: Panel display options.

parameters.name: UI Language / UI Font Size / Scale UI To Font
parameters.description: Presentation; changes need a restart.

tools.example: Right-clicking the canvas margin also sets the canvas colour without opening preferences.
tools.notes: UI scaling on Windows can be overridden per app in Windows display settings; 'Scale UI To Font' is the in-app option.

tools.name: Preferences > Workspace
tools.description: Panel and document-window behaviour: auto-collapse iconic panels, auto-show hidden panels when the pointer touches the edge, open documents as tabs, allow floating windows to dock, large tabs, condensed layout, narrow options bar, and the Restore Default Workspaces button.

parameters.name: Auto-Collapse Iconic Panels
parameters.description: Collapse an expanded icon panel when you click elsewhere.

parameters.name: Auto-Show Hidden Panels
parameters.description: Reveal panels hidden with Tab when the pointer reaches the screen edge.

parameters.name: Open Documents as Tabs / Enable Floating Document Window Docking
parameters.description: Tabbed vs floating documents.

parameters.name: Large Tabs / Condensed / Enable Narrow Options Bar
parameters.description: Density controls for small screens.

tools.example: On a 13-inch laptop tick Enable Narrow Options Bar and Condensed to reclaim space.
tools.notes: Workspaces themselves are saved from Window > Workspace > New Workspace.

tools.name: Preferences > Tools
tools.description: Tool behaviour switches: tooltips and rich tooltips, gestures, Shift-key tool cycling, overscroll, flick panning, double-click on a mask opening Select and Mask, HUD brush hardness, snapping of vector tools and transforms to the pixel grid, transform reference point display, scroll-wheel zoom, animated zoom, zoom resizing windows, zoom to clicked point, and Use Legacy Free Transform.

parameters.name: Show Tooltips / Show Rich Tooltips
parameters.description: Plain or animated tool hints.

parameters.name: Use Shift Key for Tool Switch
parameters.description: When off, pressing a tool letter cycles hidden tools without Shift.

parameters.name: Overscroll
parameters.description: Allows scrolling the image past the window edge at any zoom.

parameters.name: Snap Vector Tools and Transforms to Pixel Grid
parameters.description: Keeps shapes crisp for UI work.

parameters.name: Zoom with Scroll Wheel / Animated Zoom / Zoom Resizes Windows / Zoom Clicked Point to Center
parameters.description: Navigation behaviour.

parameters.name: Use Legacy Free Transform
parameters.description: Restores Shift = proportional for all layer types (since 20.0 proportional is the default).

parameters.name: Show Reference Point when Transforming
parameters.description: Displays the pivot in Free Transform (off by default since 20.0).

tools.example: Tick Zoom with Scroll Wheel to zoom without Ctrl; tick Show Reference Point when Transforming when you need to rotate around a moved pivot.
tools.notes: Tool-specific options (brush size, etc.) live in the options bar and tool presets, not here.

tools.name: Preferences > History & Content Credentials
tools.description: Two unrelated features share this pane: the History Log (record edits into file metadata, a text file or both, at Sessions Only, Concise or Detailed granularity) and Content Credentials (enable attaching C2PA provenance data to exports, choose connected accounts and whether to include edits/actions and producer name). The History Log is what forensic and compliance workflows use to prove edit steps.

parameters.name: History Log
parameters.description: Off/On; Save Log Items To: Metadata, Text File, Both.

parameters.name: Edit Log Items
parameters.description: Sessions Only, Concise, Detailed (includes every parameter, e.g. Curves points).

parameters.name: Content Credentials
parameters.description: Enable; attribution (name, connected Behance/Instagram/X accounts); Include: Edits and Activity, Producer.

tools.example: Turn on History Log (Detailed, Metadata) before retouching evidence photos; File > File Info > Raw Data then shows the full edit history.
tools.notes: Content Credentials require an internet connection when signing exports; supported output formats are JPEG and PNG (and PSD for preview). ExtendScript: `app.preferences.useHistoryLog`, `saveLogItems`, `editLogItems`.

tools.name: Preferences > File Handling
tools.description: Saving and compatibility: image previews/thumbnails, Save As to original folder, background saving, auto-save recovery interval, Camera Raw conversion of 32-bit files, EXIF profile handling, rotation metadata, the layered TIFF prompt, PSD compression, Maximize PSD/PSB File Compatibility (Never/Always/Ask), recent file count, and the Camera Raw Preferences button plus 'Prefer Adobe Camera Raw for Supported Raw Files'.

parameters.name: Automatically Save Recovery Information Every
parameters.description: 5-60 minutes; the recovery copies are separate from the file and used after a crash.

parameters.name: Save in Background
parameters.description: Lets you continue working while large files save.

parameters.name: Maximize PSD and PSB File Compatibility
parameters.description: Never / Always / Ask - embeds a flattened composite so other apps (Lightroom, older versions) can read the file; increases size.

parameters.name: Disable Compression of PSD and PSB Files
parameters.description: Faster saves, larger files.

parameters.name: Ignore EXIF Profile Tag / Ignore Rotation Metadata
parameters.description: Treat camera profile/orientation tags as absent.

parameters.name: Ask Before Saving Layered TIFF Files
parameters.description: Warn when TIFF will carry layers.

parameters.name: Recent File List Contains
parameters.description: 0-100 entries.

tools.example: Set Maximize Compatibility to Always if the PSDs are catalogued in Lightroom (Lightroom cannot import PSDs saved without it).
tools.notes: ExtendScript: `app.preferences.maximizeCompatibility = MaximizeCompatibility.ALWAYS`, `imagePreviews`, `appendExtension`. Camera Raw preferences opened here are shared with Bridge and Lightroom Classic.

tools.name: Preferences > Export
tools.description: Defaults for File > Export > Quick Export (format PNG/JPG/GIF, quality, transparency, location: Ask or a fixed folder next to the document) and for Export As (metadata: None or Copyright and Contact Info; colour space: Convert to sRGB and Embed Color Profile).

parameters.name: Quick Export Format
parameters.description: PNG (with/without transparency, smaller file), JPG (quality), GIF.

parameters.name: Quick Export Location
parameters.description: Ask where to export each time, or Export files to an assets folder next to the current document.

parameters.name: Metadata / Color Space
parameters.description: Applied to both Quick Export and Export As.

tools.example: Set Quick Export to PNG, location 'assets folder', then right-click any layer > Quick Export as PNG to drop cut assets next to the PSD.
tools.notes: Export As dialog settings persist separately from these defaults.

tools.name: Preferences > Performance (Memory Usage)
tools.description: The RAM slider 'Let Photoshop Use' sets how much of the available memory Photoshop may take (the Ideal Range is suggested, 70 % is the default), and the pane also shows total available RAM. Setting it above ~85 % starves the OS and other apps and can make Photoshop slower, not faster.

parameters.name: Let Photoshop Use
parameters.description: Percentage of available RAM (and MB); takes effect after restart.

tools.example: On a 32 GB machine used only for Photoshop, set 80 %; leave 70 % if you run Premiere or a browser alongside.
tools.notes: The Efficiency indicator in the status bar (choose Efficiency from the document-window menu) below 100 % means Photoshop is paging to scratch disk - add RAM or scratch space.

tools.name: Preferences > Performance (Graphics Processor Settings)
tools.description: Enables GPU acceleration ('Use Graphics Processor') and, under Advanced Settings, the Drawing Mode (Basic, Normal, Advanced), OpenCL use, anti-aliased guides and paths, 30-bit display, and image-processing acceleration. Many features (Blur Gallery, Oil Paint, Lighting Effects, Neural Filters, Select Subject, flick panning, smooth zoom, Camera Raw GPU) require the GPU to be on and supported.
tools.usage: Edit > Preferences > Performance... > Graphics Processor Settings > Use Graphics Processor / Advanced Settings...

parameters.name: Use Graphics Processor
parameters.description: Master switch; the detected GPU is listed above it.

parameters.name: Drawing Mode
parameters.description: Basic (least GPU memory), Normal, Advanced (most features).

parameters.name: Use OpenCL
parameters.description: Accelerates Blur Gallery, Smart Sharpen, Select Focus Area.

parameters.name: Anti-alias Guides and Paths / 30 Bit Display
parameters.description: Display quality options.

parameters.name: Use Legacy Compositing / Deactivate Native Canvas
parameters.description: Compatibility toggles (appear under Technology Previews or here depending on version).

tools.example: If brush lag or canvas artefacts appear after a driver update, untick Use Graphics Processor, restart, and update the GPU driver before re-enabling.
tools.notes: Requires a GPU with DirectX 12 (Windows) / Metal (Mac) and at least 1.5 GB VRAM; 4 GB+ recommended for 4K displays. Help > System Info lists the detected GPU and any 'GPU disabled' reasons.

tools.name: Preferences > Performance (History States, Cache Levels, Cache Tile Size)
tools.description: History States (1-1000, default 50) sets how many undo steps are retained, each consuming RAM/scratch; Cache Levels (1-8) controls how many downsampled pyramid levels are kept for fast zoomed-out redraw and histogram; Cache Tile Size (128K-1024K) trades small-edit responsiveness for large-brush throughput. The three preset buttons (Tall and Thin, Default, Big and Flat) choose sensible combinations.

parameters.name: History States
parameters.description: 1-1000; lower for very large documents.

parameters.name: Cache Levels
parameters.description: 1-8; higher speeds zoom-out redraw of big documents; 1 gives an exact histogram.

parameters.name: Cache Tile Size
parameters.description: 128K, 132K, 256K, 264K, 1024K, 1028K; larger tiles help big brushes on large images.

parameters.name: Optimize Cache and History for
parameters.description: Tall and Thin (many layers, small documents), Default, Big and Flat (large, few layers).

tools.example: Compositing 20-layer 8K matte paintings: History States 20, Cache Levels 6, Tile Size 1024K.
tools.notes: ExtendScript: `app.preferences.numberOfHistoryStates`, `app.preferences.imageCacheLevels`. Changes to cache take effect after restart.

tools.name: Preferences > Scratch Disks
tools.description: Chooses which drives hold Photoshop's virtual-memory scratch files and in what order. The scratch file can reach tens of gigabytes; put it on the fastest internal SSD with the most free space, not the system drive if another SSD is available. 'Scratch disks are full' errors are resolved here.
tools.usage: Edit > Preferences > Scratch Disks...   (hold Ctrl+Alt while launching Photoshop to set them before start-up)

parameters.name: Active checkboxes
parameters.description: Tick the drives to use; arrows reorder priority.

parameters.name: Free Space / Information
parameters.description: Read-only capacity readout per drive.

tools.example: Tick D: (NVMe, 800 GB free) and move it above C:, then restart.
tools.notes: Requires restart. Removable and network drives are not recommended. Edit > Purge frees RAM but not scratch; scratch files are deleted on quit.

tools.name: Preferences > Image Processing
tools.description: A newer pane that groups image-processing algorithm switches formerly scattered across General and Technology Previews, such as the default image interpolation method and legacy/compatibility processing toggles for compositing and healing. Consult it when results differ from an older machine or when a feature offers a 'legacy' behaviour.

parameters.name: Image Interpolation
parameters.description: Default resampling method for transforms (mirrors the General option in older versions).

parameters.name: Legacy / compatibility toggles
parameters.description: Version-dependent switches for older compositing or filter algorithms.

tools.example: Set the default interpolation to Preserve Details 2.0 when most Free Transforms are enlargements.
tools.notes: Pane contents vary by version (added in the 2024-2025 releases); options not present here are under General or Technology Previews.

tools.name: Preferences > Cursors
tools.description: Sets the pointer shape for painting tools (Standard icon, Precise crosshair, Normal Brush Tip = 50 % opacity outline, Full Size Brush Tip, plus Show Crosshair in Brush Tip and Show Only Crosshair While Painting) and other tools (Standard or Precise), and the colour of the brush preview shown while adjusting size/hardness on canvas.

parameters.name: Painting Cursors
parameters.description: Standard, Precise, Normal Brush Tip, Full Size Brush Tip; crosshair options.

parameters.name: Other Cursors
parameters.description: Standard or Precise.

parameters.name: Brush Preview
parameters.description: Colour of the HUD size/hardness preview.

tools.example: Choose Full Size Brush Tip with Show Crosshair in Brush Tip so soft brushes show their true extent.
tools.notes: Caps Lock toggles between the brush-tip cursor and the precise crosshair at any time - a common reason for 'my cursor changed'.

tools.name: Preferences > Transparency & Gamut
tools.description: Configures the checkerboard shown behind transparent pixels (grid size None/Small/Medium/Large and colour scheme or custom colours) and the colour and opacity of the overlay used by View > Gamut Warning.

parameters.name: Grid Size / Grid Colors
parameters.description: None hides the checkerboard (shows white); Light, Medium, Dark, Red, Orange, Green, Blue, Purple or custom swatches.

parameters.name: Gamut Warning Color / Opacity
parameters.description: Default grey at 100 %; choose a vivid colour so warnings stand out.

tools.example: Set Grid Size None when judging transparent PNG edges against white, then restore.
tools.notes: ExtendScript: `app.preferences.transparencyGridSize`, `transparencyStyle`, `gamutWarningOpacity`.

tools.name: Preferences > Units & Rulers
tools.description: Sets the ruler unit (pixels, inches, cm, mm, points, picas, percent) and the type unit (points, pixels, mm), column size and gutter used by Image Size/Canvas Size 'columns', the default resolutions offered for Print and Screen presets in New Document, and whether a point is PostScript (72/inch) or Traditional (72.27/inch).
tools.usage: Edit > Preferences > Units & Rulers...   (right-click a ruler to change the unit quickly)

parameters.name: Rulers
parameters.description: Pixels, Inches, Centimeters, Millimeters, Points, Picas, Percent.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Points, Pixels, Millimeters.

parameters.name: Column Size
parameters.description: Width and Gutter for column-based sizing.

parameters.name: New Document Preset Resolutions
parameters.description: Print Resolution (300 ppi) and Screen Resolution (72 ppi).

parameters.name: Point/Pica Size
parameters.description: PostScript (72 points/inch) or Traditional (72.27 points/inch).

tools.example:
app.preferences.rulerUnits = Units.PIXELS;
app.preferences.typeUnits = TypeUnits.PIXELS;   // set at the top of every script
tools.notes: Scripts that read `doc.width` get a UnitValue in the current ruler unit - set it explicitly to avoid surprises. Ctrl+R toggles rulers.

tools.name: Preferences > Guides, Grid & Slices
tools.description: Colours and styles for canvas guides, artboard guides, inactive artboard guides and Smart Guides; the grid colour, style (Lines, Dashed, Dots), spacing ('Gridline Every') and subdivisions; slice line colour and slice-number display; and the colour/width of the path outline overlay.

parameters.name: Guides: Canvas / Artboard / Inactive Artboard / Smart Guides
parameters.description: Colour and Lines/Dashed style per guide type; 'Show inactive artboard guides'.

parameters.name: Grid
parameters.description: Color, Style, Gridline Every (value + unit), Subdivisions.

parameters.name: Slices
parameters.description: Line Color, Show Slice Numbers.

parameters.name: Path Options
parameters.description: Colour and thickness of path outlines (Default 1 px).

tools.example: Gridline Every 8 px, Subdivisions 1, for an 8-point UI grid; View > Show > Grid (Ctrl+') to display it.
tools.notes: View > New Guide Layout creates column/row guides independent of these preferences. Guides can also be coloured individually since 2020.

tools.name: Preferences > Plugins
tools.description: Controls third-party extensions: whether legacy CEP extension panels load, whether extensions may connect to the internet, and (in older versions) an Additional Plug-ins Folder. Also holds the Filters & Extension Panels options such as 'Show all Filter Gallery groups and names' (lists every gallery filter in the Filter menu).

parameters.name: Allow Extensions to Connect to the Internet
parameters.description: Needed by extensions that phone home or download assets.

parameters.name: Load Extension Panels
parameters.description: Enable legacy CEP panels (Window > Extensions (legacy)).

parameters.name: Show all Filter Gallery groups and names
parameters.description: Expose Artistic, Brush Strokes, Sketch, Texture submenus directly in the Filter menu.

parameters.name: Enable Generator
parameters.description: Turns on the Generator engine used by File > Generate > Image Assets and generator plugins.

tools.example: Tick 'Show all Filter Gallery groups and names' so actions recorded in old versions that reference 'Filter > Artistic > Cutout' play back.
tools.notes: UXP plugins are managed from Plugins > Plugins Panel / Creative Cloud Desktop, not here. Third-party .8bf plug-ins go in Program Files/Common Files/Adobe/Plug-Ins/CC.

tools.name: Preferences > Type
tools.description: Typesetting behaviour: smart (curly) quotes, on-canvas alternate-glyph pop-up for type layers, missing-glyph protection (substitutes glyphs the current font lacks), showing font names in English, filling new type layers with placeholder text, and choosing the text engine (Latin, East Asian, Middle Eastern and South Asian).

parameters.name: Use Smart Quotes
parameters.description: Typographic quotes while typing.

parameters.name: Enable Type layer glyph alternates
parameters.description: Shows the alternates pop-up when you select a character on canvas.

parameters.name: Enable Missing Glyph Protection
parameters.description: Automatically substitutes a font for characters missing in the current font.

parameters.name: Show Font Names in English
parameters.description: For East Asian fonts.

parameters.name: Fill new type layers with placeholder text
parameters.description: Auto lorem ipsum for new paragraph boxes.

parameters.name: Choose Text Engine Options
parameters.description: Default (Latin), East Asian, Middle Eastern and South Asian.

tools.example: Untick Use Smart Quotes when typing code samples or inch marks (6'2").
tools.notes: Text engine changes apply to new type layers only.

tools.name: Preferences > Technology Previews
tools.description: Opt-in switches for features Adobe ships before they are final - past examples include Preserve Details 2.0 upscaling, Content Credentials (Beta), precise brush preview, multithreaded compositing, Deactivate Native Canvas and Enable Generative features previews. Each entry has a description link; most require a restart and can be disabled if they cause instability.

parameters.name: Feature checkboxes
parameters.description: Vary per release; each links to a help article.

tools.example: If the canvas renders blank after an update, open Technology Previews and toggle 'Deactivate Native Canvas', then restart.
tools.notes: Preview features can be removed or graduated to standard features in any release; do not build production automation on them. See Help > What's New for the list current to your version.

tools.name: Preferences > Notifications
tools.description: Controls in-app messaging: Quiet Mode silences feature introductions, What's New pop-ups and rich tooltips for a chosen duration or permanently, and individual checkboxes toggle each notification class. Useful in classrooms, kiosks and automated workstations where dialogs must not interrupt scripts.

parameters.name: Quiet Mode
parameters.description: Off / On (with duration); makes the other checkboxes read-only while on.

parameters.name: Feature introductions / What's New / Rich tooltips / Definitions on hover
parameters.description: Individual notification classes.

tools.example: Enable Quiet Mode on a render-farm workstation that runs Photoshop batch scripts unattended.
tools.notes: Available in Photoshop 2024 (25.x) and later; earlier versions had only the Interface > Show tooltips options.

tools.name: Camera Raw Preferences
tools.description: Shared preferences of the Camera Raw plug-in (used by Photoshop, Bridge and the Camera Raw Filter): where settings are stored (sidecar XMP vs database), raw defaults per camera, JPEG/HEIC/TIFF handling (whether such files open in Camera Raw), cache size and location, GPU use, and workflow defaults. Opened from File Handling or from the Camera Raw dialog's gear icon.
tools.usage: Edit > Preferences > Camera Raw... (or File Handling > Camera Raw Preferences...; Ctrl+K inside the Camera Raw dialog)

parameters.name: General > Save image settings in
parameters.description: Sidecar '.xmp' files (portable) or Camera Raw database.

parameters.name: Raw Defaults
parameters.description: Adobe Default, Camera Settings, or a preset, per camera model/serial.

parameters.name: File Handling > JPEG, HEIC and TIFF Handling
parameters.description: Disable support / Automatically open with settings / Automatically open all supported files.

parameters.name: Performance > Use Graphics Processor
parameters.description: Off / Auto / Custom (Use GPU for display, image processing, AI).

parameters.name: Cache
parameters.description: Maximum size (GB) and location of the preview cache; Purge Cache button.

parameters.name: Workflow
parameters.description: Default colour space, bit depth, size and sharpening for images opened into Photoshop (same as Workflow Options).

tools.example: Set JPEG handling to 'Automatically open all supported JPEGs' so File > Open always routes JPEGs through Camera Raw for raw-style editing.
tools.notes: Preferences are stored separately from Photoshop's and survive a Photoshop preferences reset. Bridge uses the same settings.

tools.name: Reset Preferences and the preferences file
tools.description: Corrupt preferences cause a large share of odd behaviour (missing panels, tool glitches, crashes on launch). Reset them by holding Ctrl+Alt+Shift immediately after launching Photoshop and confirming the dialog, by ticking Preferences > General > Reset Preferences On Quit, or by deleting the settings folder. Export/Import Presets (Edit > Presets) saves your brushes and actions before a reset.
tools.usage: Hold Ctrl+Alt+Shift (Mac: Cmd+Option+Shift) while Photoshop starts > 'Delete the Adobe Photoshop Settings File?' > Yes   |   Edit > Preferences > General > Reset Preferences On Quit

parameters.name: Settings location (Windows)
parameters.description: %AppData%\Adobe\Adobe Photoshop <version>\Adobe Photoshop <version> Settings\ (Adobe Photoshop <version> Prefs.psp plus workspaces, actions palette, brushes).

parameters.name: Settings location (macOS)
parameters.description: ~/Library/Preferences/Adobe Photoshop <version> Settings/.

tools.example: Before resetting: Edit > Presets > Export/Import Presets > Export to save brushes, swatches and actions; then reset and re-import.
tools.notes: Camera Raw preferences are stored separately and survive the reset. Saved workspaces, custom keyboard shortcuts and menu sets live in the settings folder and are lost unless exported first.

tools.name: Color Settings > Working Spaces
tools.description: The RGB, CMYK, Gray and Spot working spaces define the colour meaning of documents that have no embedded profile and the default profile for new documents. Typical choices: sRGB IEC61966-2.1 for web/general use, Adobe RGB (1998) or ProPhoto RGB for wide-gamut photo work, Display P3 for Apple-screen UI, and a regional press profile (U.S. Web Coated SWOP v2, Coated FOGRA39) for CMYK. Presets such as 'North America General Purpose 2' set all four at once.

parameters.name: RGB
parameters.description: sRGB, Adobe RGB (1998), ProPhoto RGB, Display P3, Monitor RGB, or any installed profile.

parameters.name: CMYK
parameters.description: Press profile matching the printer's condition.

parameters.name: Gray / Spot
parameters.description: Dot gain (10-30 %) or Gray Gamma 1.8/2.2.

parameters.name: Settings preset
parameters.description: General Purpose, Prepress, Web/Internet, Monitor Color, or Custom; Load/Save .csf files.

tools.example: Choose Settings 'Europe Prepress 3' before a magazine job: Adobe RGB working space, Coated FOGRA39 CMYK, Dot Gain 15 % Gray.
tools.notes: Bridge > Edit > Color Settings synchronises the .csf across Creative Cloud apps ('Unsynchronized' warning otherwise). Changing the working space does not alter open documents that have embedded profiles.

tools.name: Color Settings > Color Management Policies
tools.description: Decide what happens when a file's embedded profile differs from (or is missing versus) the working space: Off, Preserve Embedded Profiles (recommended) or Convert to Working RGB/CMYK/Gray, and whether to ask when profiles mismatch on open or paste or when profiles are missing. Mis-set policies are the usual cause of 'my colours changed after opening'.
tools.usage: Edit > Color Settings... > Color Management Policies

parameters.name: RGB / CMYK / Gray
parameters.description: Off, Preserve Embedded Profiles, Convert to Working <space>.

parameters.name: Profile Mismatches: Ask When Opening / Ask When Pasting
parameters.description: Show the Embedded Profile Mismatch / Paste Profile Mismatch dialogs.

parameters.name: Missing Profiles: Ask When Opening
parameters.description: Show the Missing Profile dialog instead of silently assuming the working space.

tools.example: Set all three to Preserve Embedded Profiles and tick Ask When Opening for mismatches so untagged client files can be assigned correctly.
tools.notes: When pasting between documents with different profiles, Photoshop converts colour appearance by default; untick 'Ask When Pasting' to skip the prompt.

tools.name: Color Settings > Conversion Options and Advanced Controls
tools.description: The colour engine (Adobe ACE recommended), the default rendering intent, Black Point Compensation, Dither for 8-bit conversions and Compensate for Scene-referred Profiles; the Advanced Controls add Desaturate Monitor Colors By (%), Blend RGB Colors Using Gamma (1.0 gives physically 'correct' linear blending of brushes and layers) and Blend Text Colors Using Gamma.
tools.usage: Edit > Color Settings... > tick More Options > Conversion Options / Advanced Controls

parameters.name: Engine
parameters.description: Adobe (ACE), Microsoft ICM (Windows) or Apple CMM (Mac).

parameters.name: Intent
parameters.description: Perceptual, Saturation, Relative Colorimetric (default), Absolute Colorimetric.

parameters.name: Use Black Point Compensation
parameters.description: Maps source black to destination black; leave on for printing.

parameters.name: Use Dither (8-bit/channel images)
parameters.description: Reduces banding in conversions.

parameters.name: Blend RGB Colors Using Gamma
parameters.description: 1.00 = linear-light blending (changes how soft brush edges and blend modes look); off = perceptual blending (default).

tools.example: Digital painters wanting physically plausible colour mixing enable Blend RGB Colors Using Gamma 1.00 - be aware existing files will look different.
tools.notes: Advanced options are stored in the .csf preset; document them for a team so that files render identically.

tools.name: Assign Profile
tools.description: Tags (or re-tags) the document with a colour profile without changing the pixel values, so the same numbers are interpreted as a different colour space. Use it to fix untagged or mis-tagged files (e.g. a scan that was really Adobe RGB but got labelled sRGB) - the appearance changes, the data does not.
tools.usage: Edit > Assign Profile...   |   Not in the DOM directly: use executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("assignProfile"), ...) or set Document.colorProfileName (which assigns)

parameters.name: Don't Color Manage This Document
parameters.description: Strip the profile (the working space is then assumed for display).

parameters.name: Working RGB
parameters.description: Assign the current working space.

parameters.name: Profile
parameters.description: Any installed profile; Preview toggles the on-screen effect.

tools.example: An untagged JPEG looks dull: Edit > Assign Profile > Adobe RGB (1998) - if it snaps into life, that is what it was.
tools.notes: Assign changes appearance; Convert changes numbers to keep appearance. Never use Assign to move a file to sRGB for the web - that is a Convert.

tools.name: Convert to Profile
tools.description: Recalculates the pixel values so the document looks the same in a different colour space (e.g. Adobe RGB -> sRGB for the web, RGB -> a CMYK press profile, or to a specific printer profile for a 'hard' conversion). The Advanced dialog also converts to Lab, Grayscale, Multichannel, or a device link profile, and offers Flatten Image to keep appearance when blend modes are involved.
tools.usage: Edit > Convert to Profile...   |   Document.convertProfile(destinationProfile, intent, blackPointCompensation, dither)

parameters.name: Destination Space > Profile
parameters.description: Target profile (RGB, CMYK, Gray, Lab, device link, abstract).

parameters.name: Engine / Intent / Use Black Point Compensation / Use Dither
parameters.description: Conversion options overriding Color Settings defaults.

parameters.name: Flatten Image to Preserve Appearance
parameters.description: Merges layers because blend modes and adjustments behave differently in the new space.

tools.example: app.activeDocument.convertProfile("sRGB IEC61966-2.1", Intent.RELATIVECOLORIMETRIC, true, true);   // before exporting for the web
tools.notes: Export As and Save for Web have 'Convert to sRGB' built in. Converting to CMYK is also done by Image > Mode > CMYK Color, which uses the Color Settings CMYK profile silently.

tools.name: View > Proof Setup
tools.description: Chooses the output condition to simulate on screen (soft proofing): Working CMYK, individual plates (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black, CMY), Legacy Macintosh RGB (Gamma 1.8), Internet Standard RGB (sRGB), Monitor RGB, Color Blindness (Protanopia, Deuteranopia) or Custom with any printer/press profile, intent, Black Point Compensation and Simulate Paper Color / Black Ink options. The chosen setup is what View > Proof Colors toggles.
tools.usage: View > Proof Setup > Custom... / Working CMYK / ... / Color Blindness - Protanopia-type

parameters.name: Device to Simulate
parameters.description: Any installed output profile (e.g. the lab's paper profile).

parameters.name: Preserve RGB/CMYK Numbers
parameters.description: Show how the raw numbers would look without conversion.

parameters.name: Rendering Intent + Black Point Compensation
parameters.description: How out-of-gamut colours are mapped.

parameters.name: Simulate Paper Color / Simulate Black Ink
parameters.description: Show the paper white and the limited black of the printer (most realistic, most alarming).

parameters.name: Load / Save
parameters.description: Proof setups as .psf files, which then appear in the menu.

tools.example: View > Proof Setup > Custom: Device 'Epson SC-P900 Hot Press Bright', Relative Colorimetric, BPC on, Simulate Paper Color; then View > Proof Colors (Ctrl+Y) and adjust with a Curves layer until the proof looks right.
tools.notes: Proof Colors and Gamut Warning use this setup. Also see Print dialog > Hard Proofing.

tools.name: View > Proof Colors
tools.description: Toggles the soft-proof preview defined in Proof Setup so the monitor simulates the printer, press or alternate RGB space. The document tab shows the proof profile name in parentheses while active. Use it to adjust an image for a specific output without converting it.
tools.example: Ctrl+Y on and off while editing a saturated photo destined for newsprint reveals how much saturation will be lost.
tools.notes: Proofing is per document window; New Window for the same document (Window > Arrange) lets you view proofed and unproofed side by side.

tools.name: View > Gamut Warning
tools.description: Overlays a flat colour (set in Preferences > Transparency & Gamut) on every pixel that the current proof profile cannot reproduce, so you can see where CMYK or a printer will clip saturated colours. Pair with Hue/Saturation or Selective Color layers to tame those regions.
tools.example: Proof Setup > Working CMYK, then Ctrl+Shift+Y: the grey overlay shows which neon greens will print dull.
tools.notes: The Color Picker and Info panel also show a small gamut-warning triangle for CMYK gamut and a cube for web-safe colours.

tools.name: Rendering intents (Perceptual, Relative Colorimetric, Saturation, Absolute Colorimetric)
tools.description: The four ICC strategies for mapping colours between gamuts. Perceptual compresses the whole gamut smoothly (good for saturated photos going to a small gamut); Relative Colorimetric keeps in-gamut colours exact and clips the rest, mapping white to paper white (default, best for most work); Saturation favours vividness over accuracy (charts); Absolute Colorimetric also reproduces the paper white for proofing on brighter stock.
tools.usage: Chosen in Edit > Color Settings, Convert to Profile, Proof Setup, Print > Color Management and Document.convertProfile(Intent.PERCEPTUAL | RELATIVECOLORIMETRIC | SATURATION | ABSOLUTECOLORIMETRIC)
tools.example: Soft-proof with both Perceptual and Relative Colorimetric and pick whichever loses less; Black Point Compensation should stay on with Relative.
tools.notes: Perceptual behaviour depends on the destination profile (v2 vs v4, table-based vs matrix); matrix (display) profiles only support colorimetric intents.

tools.name: Embed Color Profile (Save As / Export option)
tools.description: The 'ICC Profile' / 'Embed Color Profile' checkbox in Save As, Save a Copy and Export As writes the document's profile into the file so other applications interpret the colours correctly. Always embed for print and wide-gamut files; for sRGB web assets embedding is optional (browsers assume sRGB) and costs about 3 KB.
tools.usage: File > Save As... > ICC Profile: <name>   |   File > Export > Export As > Embed Color Profile   |   JPEGSaveOptions.embedColorProfile = true
tools.notes: Save for Web (Legacy) strips the profile unless 'Embed Color Profile' is ticked and 'Convert to sRGB' handles the conversion.

tools.name: View > 32-bit Preview Options
tools.description: For HDR (32-bit/channel) documents, sets how the unbounded floating-point values are mapped to the display: Exposure and Gamma sliders, or Highlight Compression, so you can inspect different tonal ranges without changing the data. The Exposure slider also lives in the document window's status bar for 32-bit files.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Exposure and Gamma, or Highlight Compression.

parameters.name: Exposure / Gamma
parameters.description: Preview-only sliders (does not alter pixels).

tools.example: Open an OpenEXR render, View > 32-bit Preview Options, Exposure -2 to check highlight detail, then Image > Mode > 8 Bits/Channel with HDR Toning to bake a look.
tools.notes: Many filters and adjustment layers are unavailable in 32-bit; the preview setting is stored with the document.

tools.name: Content Credentials panel
tools.description: Photoshop's implementation of the C2PA open standard: when enabled, exported JPEG/PNG files carry a cryptographically signed manifest listing the producer, connected social accounts, the edits and AI tools used (Generative Fill is always disclosed) and optionally a thumbnail. The panel previews the credential before export and links to Adobe Content Authenticity for inspection and cloud-stored credentials.
tools.usage: Window > Content Credentials (Beta)   |   enable in Edit > Preferences > History & Content Credentials   |   Export As / Save a Copy: Content Credentials option

parameters.name: Enable Content Credentials
parameters.description: Per document toggle once enabled in preferences.

parameters.name: Attribution
parameters.description: Producer name and connected Behance/Instagram/X/LinkedIn accounts.

parameters.name: Include
parameters.description: Edits and activity (categories of edits, AI usage), Producer, Thumbnail.

parameters.name: Publish to cloud
parameters.description: Store the credential in Adobe's cloud so it survives metadata stripping (recoverable by fingerprint).

tools.example: Preferences > History & Content Credentials > enable; Window > Content Credentials (Beta) > preview; File > Export > Export As > JPEG with Content Credentials: Attach; verify at contentcredentials.org/verify.
tools.notes: Requires sign-in and internet for signing. Any pixel edit after export invalidates the signature. Generative AI outputs are always labelled in the credential even if other edits are omitted.
